get.description:
The readings the values settled with no question asked, each with its evidence and the
answers that change it ("read from your data"; BLUEPRINT §14.3). Nothing waits on them.

The quest log's seven stages, in order (SIZING P0.4): each stage's lines under Decide,
Confirm and For the record, with "Waiting for" on a line whose earlier answers are missing;
progress as answered over required, null for a stage not reached, with ``complete`` once every
objective is answered (a reached stage that asks nothing, 0 of 0, is complete: its segment is
full); and, when an answer decided in another stage asked its questions again or left its
results out of date, or another answer in the stage itself asked its questions again
(``within``), why, in plain words. ``version`` changes when the shape or the meaning of this
log does.

post.description:
Fit, pressed on the analysis flowchart (SIZING P0.8; RECIPES_AND_TUNING §4.4): a job
command, not a decision. It releases a fit the scheduler holds (one expected to take over
about 2 minutes) and opens Results. Under Estimate and Describe it locks the analysis plan, the
system's ``lock_plan`` record, once; no estimate is served before it. Under Predict nothing
locks, and no score or estimate is served before it. Refused while nothing is chosen to fit or
a question the estimates rest on is open. Returns the lock as the quest log shows it.

409.description: Nothing to fit yet, or a question the estimates rest on is open

post.description:
Cancel, where Fit was on the analysis flowchart (calm/FOUNDATION §7): the estimates' work
still running stops. Before any estimate is served the press is withdrawn, and under Estimate
and Describe the plan's lock with it (kept in the record as withdrawn), so Fit is asked for
again; once an estimate has been served the lock stands. Returns the lock as the quest log
shows it.

get.description:
The manuscript bundle: the methods section from the record (ordered by STROBE or
TRIPOD+AI), the participant-flow and lineage figures as journal-format SVG, the results tables
as CSV and Markdown, the filled checklist, the analysis plan with its SHA-256 and the
provenance record a replay checks (``python -m turbotab.replay``). Refused while a required
question is unanswered, the plan is open, an input file changed or a result is not computed.

get.description:
The reporting checklist of the declared purpose (STROBE-nut under inference, TRIPOD+AI
under prediction): every item quoted from its source, with where the record answers it or
"unanswered — the author must supply this", and what the export still waits for. Reading it
records nothing, so it shows no score that was not already shown: under prediction the
declared result is quoted only once the fit's cross-validated scores have been shown.

ApplyRepair-Input.title: ApplyRepair
ApplyRepair-Input.description:
Apply one of a finding's repair options. Row-local repairs rewrite the working table now;
statistical ones are recorded and executed in-fold (lockbox constitution §06).

ApplyRepair-Output.description:
Apply one of a finding's repair options. Row-local repairs rewrite the working table now;

AskCard.title: AskCard
AskCard.description: "Tell me about these columns", in the question whose answer feeds the consumer.

AskGroup.title: AskGroup
AskGroup.description: One line of the card: a reading, or a homogeneous family of them confirmed as one block.

AskSettled.title: AskSettled
AskSettled.description:
One reading the values settled for this consumer, no question asked
(``readings.read_from_data``, the readings endpoint's own item).

CausalSpec.title: CausalSpec
CausalSpec.description:
The causal lane's answer for one exposure: the estimator (or none beside the primary), its
nuisance learner (None: the default for the table's size), whose effect (everyone, or the
exposed), the cross-fitting folds and sample splits, and the assumptions declared before any
estimate. ``trim``: keep the rows whose propensity lies in [trim, 1 − trim] (the overlap
population); ``acknowledged``: every row kept although positivity is practically violated;
``sample_only``: unweighted under a survey design, for these participants (block and record);
``complete_rows``: the complete rows only, where the missing-values answer fills or imputes.

Caution.title: Caution
Caution.description:
A concern the preview itself shows, inside the stage, with the control that acts on it
(DESIGN_LANGUAGE §09: a caveat arrives with its lever, in the same place).

ChecklistReport.title: ChecklistReport
ChecklistReport.description: A reporting checklist, every item listed with where the bundle answers it.

ClusterSpec.title: ClusterSpec
ClusterSpec.description:
The cluster answer: the column grouping participants (a site, a centre, a household, a
batch), or None when nothing groups them; under inference how the model takes it.

CoachAnchor.title: CoachAnchor

CodebookConflict-Input.title: CodebookConflict
CodebookConflict-Input.description:
A codebook field the values contradict, or one whose check cannot run here (``checked``
False: a check that cannot run confirms nothing): asked, never applied (BLUEPRINT
§14.2–§14.3).

CodebookConflict-Output.title: CodebookConflict
CodebookConflict-Output.description:
A codebook field the values contradict, or one whose check cannot run here (``checked``
False: a check that cannot run confirms nothing): asked, never applied (BLUEPRINT
§14.2–§14.3).

CodebookPreview.title: CodebookPreview
CodebookPreview.description:
What importing a codebook would do (``import_codebook`` with this ``id`` records it): the
readings its structured fields settle, its documented units, how many labels it gives, the
fields the values contradict (asked, never applied), the readings the user answered
otherwise (kept), and the sentence it would record.

CodebookRequest.title: CodebookRequest
CodebookRequest.description:
A codebook to read: a file on this machine (local mode only), or the variable labels the
table's own SAS transport files carry (``labels``).

CodebookSpec.title: CodebookSpec
CodebookSpec.description:
One imported codebook as the state keeps it (``codebooks`` slot, keyed by its id):
``settled`` the readings its structured fields settled (``"<kind>:<column>"`` -> value),
``units`` the documented units no reading kind takes (``mg/dL``; a sentence may state them),
``labels`` its free-text labels of the table's columns (they only strengthen a guess),
``asked`` its fields the values contradict, ``kept`` the readings the user had answered
otherwise before (the user's answer stands).

ColumnUnitSpec.title: ColumnUnitSpec
ColumnUnitSpec.description:
A column's recorded unit and, for total energy, the number of days each value totals: the
one place both readings are kept (BLUEPRINT §14.3, every confirmation is honored), written by
``set_column_unit`` (both in one answer) and by ``confirm_reading`` / ``confirm_readings`` for a
unit or a day count (each merged into what was recorded before). ``None``: not recorded.

ConfirmReading.title: ConfirmReading
ConfirmReading.description:
One reading of the data, confirmed on its own after its evidence was read (BLUEPRINT §14.1:
"Confirmation is one reading at a time, never a bulk confirm of uncertain readings"). One
column, one kind and one value per record: a role (``exposure``), whether a column's
repeating values cluster the rows (``yes``/``no``), a unit (``kg``), the days a total-energy
value spans (``2``), whether whole numbers are codes or amounts, or that a column orders a
unit's rows. ``confirm_role`` records stay valid: each is this decision's role kind.

ConfirmReadings.title: ConfirmReadings
ConfirmReadings.description:
A block confirmation (BLUEPRINT §14.2: "A block confirmation settles exactly the readings
it lists, each with the value it shows. It never settles a reading it does not list."): the
readings a question listed, each with its best guess as shown (or as the user changed it),
recorded exactly as ``confirm_reading`` records each one. One record, so one revert undoes it.

ConfirmRole.title: ConfirmRole
ConfirmRole.description:
One column's role, confirmed on its own after its evidence was read (BLUEPRINT §14 rule 2:
a proposal below high "needs its own confirmation; it never rides along in a bulk 'confirm
all'"). One column per record, so an individual confirmation is individual by construction.

CovariateAnswers-Input.title: CovariateAnswers
CovariateAnswers-Input.description:
The modified disjunctive cause criterion, asked as questions (VanderWeele 2019; MODELING_
SEQUENCE §1 step 3). The covariate's role is derived from these, never chosen directly.

CovariateAnswers-Output.title: CovariateAnswers
CovariateAnswers-Output.description:
The modified disjunctive cause criterion, asked as questions (VanderWeele 2019; MODELING_
SEQUENCE §1 step 3). The covariate's role is derived from these, never chosen directly.

CreateProject.title: CreateProject
CreateProject.description: Open a file on this machine by its path (local mode only).

DeferFinding.title: DeferFinding
DeferFinding.description: Hold a finding until the question it belongs to; it resurfaces there, attributed.

EstimandSpec.title: EstimandSpec
EstimandSpec.description:
The exposure and the effect the inference reports (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 2): one
exposure, or an exposure family (``family``: every exposure-role column, each reported, with
its multiplicity method; ``exposure`` is then None).

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: A pack's badge: where the field stands, and the section that says so.

ExposureFormSpec-Input.title: ExposureFormSpec
ExposureFormSpec-Input.description:
How one numeric predictor enters the models: a straight line, a restricted cubic spline
(``knots`` 3–5, at Harrell's percentiles; ``knots_rule`` "harrell" when k was set by the
declared rule on ``n_effective``), quintile indicators with a trend test, indicators at declared
cut points (``cuts``), one data-derived cut point, or, for an exposure with a mass at zero,
non-consumers as their own category beside a spline among consumers. ``domain`` "consumers"
restricts the analysis to consumers (an estimand change, STROBE-nut nut-14). ``acknowledged``
keeps a blocked-and-recorded form as a recorded limitation. ``scale`` is the exposure's
transform as it stood when the form was declared (``methods.exposure_form.transform_signature``):
a later transform makes the form stale, re-asked and never kept. ``unit`` is the unit the
estimate is per, on that scale (the estimand's unit).

ExposureFormSpec-Output.title: ExposureFormSpec
ExposureFormSpec-Output.description:
How one numeric predictor enters the models: a straight line, a restricted cubic spline
(``knots`` 3–5, at Harrell's percentiles; ``knots_rule`` "harrell" when k was set by the
declared rule on ``n_effective``), quintile indicators with a trend test, indicators at declared
cut points (``cuts``), one data-derived cut point, or, for an exposure with a mass at zero,
non-consumers as their own category beside a spline among consumers. ``domain`` "consumers"
restricts the analysis to consumers (an estimand change, STROBE-nut nut-14). ``acknowledged``
keeps a blocked-and-recorded form as a recorded limitation. ``scale`` is the exposure's
transform as it stood when the form was declared (``methods.exposure_form.transform_signature``):
a later transform makes the form stale, re-asked and never kept. ``unit`` is the unit the
estimate is per, on that scale (the estimand's unit).

FeatureTableSpec.title: FeatureTableSpec
FeatureTableSpec.description: How a features-in-rows table's columns read before it is turned (audit MA-04).

FitLock.title: FitLock
FitLock.description:
Fit and the plan's lock, as the quest log shows them (FOUNDATION §7: "Plan fixed at 14:02",
with the plan's SHA-256 as its quiet label).

FollowUpSpec.title: FollowUpSpec
FollowUpSpec.description:
How long each row of a time-to-event outcome was observed (WP12,
``turbotab/core/models/survival.py``): at risk from ``entry`` (0 when not named) to ``time``,
when the event happened or follow-up ended without it, both on one time scale.

GoldbergRule-Input.title: GoldbergRule
GoldbergRule-Input.description:
Keep rows whose reported energy intake over estimated BMR lies within the Goldberg cut-offs
(Goldberg et al. 1991, revised by Black 2000): ``PAL × exp(±2 S / 100)`` at n = 1, with
``S = √(CV²_wEI / d + CV²_wB + CV²_tP)``. Every input is stated: the BMR equation, the PAL (one
value, or one per level of an activity column), and the days of intake the energy averages.

GoldbergRule-Output.title: GoldbergRule
GoldbergRule-Output.description:
Keep rows whose reported energy intake over estimated BMR lies within the Goldberg cut-offs
(Goldberg et al. 1991, revised by Black 2000): ``PAL × exp(±2 S / 100)`` at n = 1, with
``S = √(CV²_wEI / d + CV²_wB + CV²_tP)``. Every input is stated: the BMR equation, the PAL (one
value, or one per level of an activity column), and the days of intake the energy averages.

user.title: User
user.description: Server mode: the signed-in user; null in local mode

auth.title: Auth
auth.description: How users sign in: none (local mode), password, or proxy (the institution's single sign-on)

ImportCodebook-Input.title: ImportCodebook
ImportCodebook-Input.description:
Import the researcher's own data dictionary (Nolan, 2026-10-03; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a
variable/label/unit/codes table, an NHANES codebook page, or the labels an XPT file carries.
Its structured fields (units, value-code tables, the variable type) settle readings as the
user's own documentation, through the confirmation path ``confirm_readings`` writes; its
free-text labels only strengthen the guesses the ask leads with; a field the values contradict
is asked, never applied. The client names the staged codebook; everything else is the
server's, read from the codebook and the values.

ImportCodebook-Output.title: ImportCodebook
ImportCodebook-Output.description:
Import the researcher's own data dictionary (Nolan, 2026-10-03; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a
variable/label/unit/codes table, an NHANES codebook page, or the labels an XPT file carries.
Its structured fields (units, value-code tables, the variable type) settle readings as the
user's own documentation, through the confirmation path ``confirm_readings`` writes; its
free-text labels only strengthen the guesses the ask leads with; a field the values contradict
is asked, never applied. The client names the staged codebook; everything else is the
server's, read from the codebook and the values.

JoinCounts-Input.title: JoinCounts
JoinCounts-Input.description:
What the join's preview counted, recorded with the answer (the server's): the rows on each
side, the identifier values they share, the rows with no partner on each side, and the rows
the joined table holds.

JoinCounts-Output.title: JoinCounts
JoinCounts-Output.description:
What the join's preview counted, recorded with the answer (the server's): the rows on each
side, the identifier values they share, the rows with no partner on each side, and the rows
the joined table holds.

JoinFiles-Input.title: JoinFiles
JoinFiles-Input.description:
Join a file added to the project to the table on a shared identifier (NHANES ships each
component as its own file, joined on ``SEQN``). ``how``: ``left`` keeps every row of the
table (a row with no partner holds blanks in the file's columns), ``inner`` only the rows with
one. One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-one are joined; many-to-many is refused with its
reason. ``name`` and ``counts`` are the server's, never the client's: the preview's counts,
recorded with the answer.

JoinFiles-Output.title: JoinFiles
JoinFiles-Output.description:
Join a file added to the project to the table on a shared identifier (NHANES ships each
component as its own file, joined on ``SEQN``). ``how``: ``left`` keeps every row of the
table (a row with no partner holds blanks in the file's columns), ``inner`` only the rows with
one. One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-one are joined; many-to-many is refused with its
reason. ``name`` and ``counts`` are the server's, never the client's: the preview's counts,
recorded with the answer.

JoinPreview.title: JoinPreview
JoinPreview.description:
What a join would do before it is committed: each side's rows and identifier values, the
relation (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one; many-to-many is refused), the rows with no
partner on each side, the joined table's rows, its new and renamed columns, and the sentence
the join would record.

JoinPreviewRequest.title: JoinPreviewRequest
JoinPreviewRequest.description:
The join to count: the added file, the identifier (``right_on`` when the file names it
otherwise), and which rows the joined table keeps.

JoinSpec.title: JoinSpec
JoinSpec.description: One file joined to the table (``joins`` slot, keyed by the file's id, in answer order).

LevelValues.title: LevelValues
LevelValues.description: A number per level of another column (a PAL per activity category).

LockPlan-Input.title: LockPlan
LockPlan-Input.description:
The inference analysis-plan lock (audit WP16, RO-12; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 12).

Recorded by the server when Fit is pressed (SIZING P0.8; before P0.8, when inference
estimates were first displayed), never posted by a client: the plan in force then is what was
declared in the software before any estimate was displayed, and every later decision is marked
as made after the estimates were seen. ``plan``
(every slot the estimates read, as it stood) and ``digest`` (its SHA-256) are filled by the
server. A client never undoes it; the server withdraws it (a revert it records itself) only
while no estimate has been served under it, on Cancel or a change to the plan
(calm/FOUNDATION §7), and the next press of Fit records a new one.

LockPlan-Output.title: LockPlan
LockPlan-Output.description:
The inference analysis-plan lock (audit WP16, RO-12; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 12).

Recorded by the server when Fit is pressed (SIZING P0.8; before P0.8, when inference
estimates were first displayed), never posted by a client: the plan in force then is what was
declared in the software before any estimate was displayed, and every later decision is marked
as made after the estimates were seen. ``plan``
(every slot the estimates read, as it stood) and ``digest`` (its SHA-256) are filled by the
server. A client never undoes it; the server withdraws it (a revert it records itself) only
while no estimate has been served under it, on Cancel or a change to the plan
(calm/FOUNDATION §7), and the next press of Fit records a new one.

Mark.title: Mark
Mark.description: A labeled value on a distribution's axis, e.g. an exclusion cut-off ("500 kcal").

MethodsLine.title: MethodsLine
MethodsLine.description: One record's sentence in the methods text.

MethodsText.title: MethodsText
MethodsText.description: The methods text: the sentences in record order, and the same joined as one paragraph.

MissingSpec.title: MissingSpec
MissingSpec.description:
The missing-values answer: columns left out of the predictors, then a strategy for the rest.

``m``: the imputations under multiple imputation. ``below_detection`` and ``censored_columns``:
how the blanks of columns whose values lie below a detection limit are filled. ``acknowledged``
and ``reason``: the recorded attestation that keeps a blocked answer (a single fill or the
missing-indicator method under inference; a median fill of non-detections, with its reason).

ModelSequenceSpec.title: ModelSequenceSpec
ModelSequenceSpec.description:
The declared adjustment sequence beside the primary model (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11):
Model 1's columns (the field's age, sex and energy, as the user names them), declared for one
exposure (or the family's ``*``). The crude model, Model 2 (the primary, the full adjustment
set) and Model 3 (plus the possible mediators the adjustment answers set beside it) follow from
the answers already given.

ModificationSpec.title: ModificationSpec
ModificationSpec.description:
One declared modifier or second exposure (``turbotab.core.methods.interaction``).

``exposure`` is the declared exposure the analysis is about (it holds while that is the
exposure); ``low`` and ``high`` its contrast on its final scale (None: the interquartile
contrast, stated); ``levels`` a numeric modifier's stated values (None: its 25th and 75th
percentiles). ``answers`` are the disjunctive cause criterion's answers for the second exposure
of an interaction. ``post_hoc``: suggested by data inspection (declared after the estimates
were seen, or so marked); it counts in the family either way. ``withdrawn``: withdrawn after
the estimates were seen: no longer estimated, its heterogeneity test still counted in the
family the record states (the analyst saw it).

Named.title: Named
Named.description:
A term or phenomenon in two registers (C5): the card's plain sentence, and the quiet name
with its source, shown on point or focus, never as a second label.

OpenSeal-Input.title: OpenSeal
OpenSeal-Input.description:
Open the held-out rows: once, at the end. Held-out scores are withheld until then.

``family`` is the final model, declared on cross-validation before any held-out score is seen
(AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP8, ME-13; ``turbotab/core/models/selection.py``): its held-out score is the
reported result. Required when several families are fitted; with one, the opening declares it.
Null only in records from before the rule.

OpenSeal-Output.title: OpenSeal
OpenSeal-Output.description:
Open the held-out rows: once, at the end. Held-out scores are withheld until then.

``family`` is the final model, declared on cross-validation before any held-out score is seen
(AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP8, ME-13; ``turbotab/core/models/selection.py``): its held-out score is the
reported result. Required when several families are fitted; with one, the opening declares it.
Null only in records from before the rule.

PlanExport.title: PlanExport
PlanExport.description: The exported analysis plan: the plan, when it was declared, its hash and its text.

Progress.title: Progress
Progress.description:
A reached stage's objectives: each counted Decide one, its Confirm sweep one. ``complete``
once every one is answered. A reached stage that asks nothing (0 of 0: First look until its
noticings are wired, Results under Estimate, Write-up) is complete, its segment full; a stage
not reached has no progress at all (empty, never "0 of N").

ProjectState.title: ProjectState
ProjectState.description: The fold of the decision log. Later milestones add slots as fields.

QuestLine.title: QuestLine
QuestLine.description:
One line of a stage: a Router question, a declaration or a finding.

``status``: ``answered``; ``open`` (answerable now); ``waiting`` (``waiting_for`` names the
earlier answers it needs, ``computing`` the results its card waits for); ``set_for_you`` (a
default the engine stated, in the Confirm sweep or For the record).

QuestLog.title: QuestLog
QuestLog.description:
The seven stages, each with its lines, progress and reopen reasons; ``kinds`` places every
decision kind (a methods sentence's "change" link opens its stage, disagreement 19; a revert
sits with the record it undoes).

RangeByLevel.title: RangeByLevel
RangeByLevel.description: Different plausible ranges per level of another column (e.g. by sex).

ReadFromData.title: ReadFromData
ReadFromData.description:
One reading the values settled with no question asked (BLUEPRINT §14.3, amendment:
settlement is visible), with its evidence and the answers that change it.

ReadingItem.title: ReadingItem
ReadingItem.description: One reading a block confirmation lists, with the value it shows.

ReadingsCard.title: ReadingsCard
ReadingsCard.description:
The readings card's "read from your data": every reading the values settled, never a
required tap, and the methods record's line for them.

Refusal.title: Refusal
Refusal.description: Every error the API answers itself; HTTP 409 when a decision is refused.

RelationshipView.title: RelationshipView
RelationshipView.description: A before/after scatter, e.g. a nutrient against energy before and after adjustment.

Reopened.title: Reopened
Reopened.description:
Why a stage dropped back: an answer decided in another stage asked its questions again or
left its results computed for other answers; or (``within``) another answer in the stage
itself asked its questions again.

ReopenedBy.title: ReopenedBy
ReopenedBy.description: The record whose change asked a line again, and the stage it was decided in.

Reseal-Input.title: Reseal
Reseal-Input.description:
Draw the held-out rows again after they were opened (audit WP16, RO-05).

Once opened, the held-out rows hold still: a new seed or holdout, or anything else that would
draw them again, waits for this recorded re-seal. It withdraws the opening of the current
outcome's seal, so the rows drawn next are withheld until they are opened in turn; the scores
at the first opening stay the reported result, and later held-out scores are not an
independent test. ``target`` is filled by the server. It stands while its outcome is the
target, as the opening does.

Reseal-Output.title: Reseal
Reseal-Output.description:
Draw the held-out rows again after they were opened (audit WP16, RO-05).

Once opened, the held-out rows hold still: a new seed or holdout, or anything else that would
draw them again, waits for this recorded re-seal. It withdraws the opening of the current
outcome's seal, so the rows drawn next are withheld until they are opened in turn; the scores
at the first opening stay the reported result, and later held-out scores are not an
independent test. ``target`` is filled by the server. It stands while its outcome is the
target, as the opening does.

RespondDiagnostic.title: RespondDiagnostic
RespondDiagnostic.description: The recorded response to a failed diagnostic of the primary model (``models/effects.py``).

RowStep.title: RowStep
RowStep.description: One step of the participant flow (CONSORT/STROBE style).

ScaleSpec-Input.title: ScaleSpec
ScaleSpec-Input.description:
One scale: its items, the instrument's key (the reverse-coded items and the response scale
``low``–``high`` they are turned over on), how the score is formed, what kind of construct it
measures (``reflective``: the items are caused by it; ``formative``: an index defined by its
components, such as a diet-quality score), its structure, the role the score takes in the
models, and whether its coefficient is corrected for measurement error, from which reliability.

ScaleSpec-Output.title: ScaleSpec
ScaleSpec-Output.description:
One scale: its items, the instrument's key (the reverse-coded items and the response scale
``low``–``high`` they are turned over on), how the score is formed, what kind of construct it
measures (``reflective``: the items are caused by it; ``formative``: an index defined by its
components, such as a diet-quality score), its structure, the role the score takes in the
models, and whether its coefficient is corrected for measurement error, from which reliability.

SealCells.title: SealCells
SealCells.description:
The seal drawn one cell per row (M2_CONTRACT §3, §11): which side each row falls on and which
unit it belongs to, so the basis is a picture. Whole units, in file order, up to
:data:`SEAL_CELLS` rows; the counts are over every row the seal is drawn from. No outcome value
is carried: only row identity, the draw, and (chronological) each unit's last time.

SensitivityAnalysis-Input.title: SensitivityAnalysis
SensitivityAnalysis-Input.description: One analysis beside the primary: the same model on the rows these rules keep instead.

SensitivityAnalysis-Output.title: SensitivityAnalysis
SensitivityAnalysis-Output.description: One analysis beside the primary: the same model on the rows these rules keep instead.

SetAdjustment-Input.title: SetAdjustment
SetAdjustment-Input.description:
Answers for some covariates, against one exposure: one tap per group of covariates that
share their answers (BLUEPRINT §14.2). Each covariate's answer is kept under its column, so a
later group's answers never undo an earlier group's.

SetAdjustment-Output.title: SetAdjustment
SetAdjustment-Output.description:
Answers for some covariates, against one exposure: one tap per group of covariates that
share their answers (BLUEPRINT §14.2). Each covariate's answer is kept under its column, so a
later group's answers never undo an earlier group's.

SetBatch-Input.title: SetBatch
SetBatch-Input.description:
How a batch column is handled, by purpose (``turbotab.core.methods.batch``). ``figures``
adds ComBat with the outcome protected for figures only: never the matrix the tests read.

SetBatch-Output.title: SetBatch
SetBatch-Output.description:
How a batch column is handled, by purpose (``turbotab.core.methods.batch``). ``figures``
adds ComBat with the outcome protected for figures only: never the matrix the tests read.

SetCategorical.title: SetCategorical
SetCategorical.description:
Columns whose numbers are codes for categories (RIDRETH3: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7): each enters
the models as indicators, one per level after the first, never as one straight line.

SetCensoring-Input.title: SetCensoring
SetCensoring-Input.description:
The follow-up question's "no" (audit RO-03): nobody's follow-up ended before the event could
be seen, so the yes/no outcome counts events over one period for everyone. Stands only while
``column`` is the target. Follow-up that varies is a time to event instead (``set_task``, then
``set_follow_up``). ``acknowledged``: kept although a column reads as a follow-up time that
varies (block and record).

SetCensoring-Output.title: SetCensoring
SetCensoring-Output.description:
The follow-up question's "no" (audit RO-03): nobody's follow-up ended before the event could
be seen, so the yes/no outcome counts events over one period for everyone. Stands only while
``column`` is the target. Follow-up that varies is a time to event instead (``set_task``, then
``set_follow_up``). ``acknowledged``: kept although a column reads as a follow-up time that
varies (block and record).

SetClusters-Input.title: SetClusters
SetClusters-Input.description:
The grouping above the person (audit RO-08). The answer is also each named column's
``cluster`` reading (BLUEPRINT §14.3): a grouping confirms it, "nothing groups them" denies
each column that read as one (``none_of``, filled by the server), and a later confirmation of
that reading stands over it, as the answer stands over an earlier one.

SetClusters-Output.title: SetClusters
SetClusters-Output.description:
The grouping above the person (audit RO-08). The answer is also each named column's
``cluster`` reading (BLUEPRINT §14.3): a grouping confirms it, "nothing groups them" denies
each column that read as one (``none_of``, filled by the server), and a later confirmation of
that reading stands over it, as the answer stands over an earlier one.

SetColumnUnit-Input.title: SetColumnUnit
SetColumnUnit-Input.description:
A column's unit, as the user reads it from the source's data dictionary, where TurboTab
could only propose one: total energy in kcal or kJ (a day's, or a total over ``days`` days),
or an age in years, months, weeks or days. Leash (BLUEPRINT §11.3): a unit not read from a
stated suffix, a codebook or the values' own agreement is a proposal, and no screen, band or
count is applied in it until it is recorded here.

SetColumnUnit-Output.title: SetColumnUnit
SetColumnUnit-Output.description:
A column's unit, as the user reads it from the source's data dictionary, where TurboTab
could only propose one: total energy in kcal or kJ (a day's, or a total over ``days`` days),
or an age in years, months, weeks or days. Leash (BLUEPRINT §11.3): a unit not read from a
stated suffix, a codebook or the values' own agreement is a proposal, and no screen, band or
count is applied in it until it is recorded here.

SetEvent.title: SetEvent
SetEvent.description: Which level of a binary outcome is the event. Stands only while ``column`` is the target.

SetExclusions-Input.title: SetExclusions
SetExclusions-Input.description: Row exclusions; an empty list is the answer "keep every row".

SetExclusions-Output.title: SetExclusions
SetExclusions-Output.description: Row exclusions; an empty list is the answer "keep every row".

SetExposureForm-Input.title: SetExposureForm
SetExposureForm-Input.description:
The form of one predictor (``turbotab.core.methods.exposure_form``); one entry per column.
Left without ``knots``, a spline takes k by the declared rule on the analyzed rows (the
completion records it); ``scale`` and ``unit`` are the server's.

SetExposureForm-Output.title: SetExposureForm
SetExposureForm-Output.description:
The form of one predictor (``turbotab.core.methods.exposure_form``); one entry per column.
Left without ``knots``, a spline takes k by the declared rule on the analyzed rows (the
completion records it); ``scale`` and ``unit`` are the server's.

SetFeatureTable-Input.title: SetFeatureTable
SetFeatureTable-Input.description:
How a features-in-rows table reads: the column naming the features, and the columns that
describe them (m/z, retention time, IDs). Turning it makes every other column a sample.

SetFeatureTable-Output.title: SetFeatureTable
SetFeatureTable-Output.description:
How a features-in-rows table reads: the column naming the features, and the columns that
describe them (m/z, retention time, IDs). Turning it makes every other column a sample.

SetFollowUp-Input.title: SetFollowUp
SetFollowUp-Input.description:
The follow-up of a time-to-event outcome. Stands only while ``column`` is the target.

``landmark``: follow-up counted from this time on (a landmark, or the customary "the first
years of follow-up excluded" for reverse causation): a row whose follow-up ended at or before
it, by an event or not, was not at risk then and leaves, and every other row is at risk from
it (left truncation; the estimate is among those event-free and followed at the landmark).
``horizon``: follow-up ends at this time: an event after it counts as censored at it.
``prediction_horizon`` (MS6): the time predicted risks are scored and calibrated at; it changes
no row.

SetFollowUp-Output.title: SetFollowUp
SetFollowUp-Output.description:
The follow-up of a time-to-event outcome. Stands only while ``column`` is the target.

``landmark``: follow-up counted from this time on (a landmark, or the customary "the first
years of follow-up excluded" for reverse causation): a row whose follow-up ended at or before
it, by an event or not, was not at risk then and leaves, and every other row is at risk from
it (left truncation; the estimate is among those event-free and followed at the landmark).
``horizon``: follow-up ends at this time: an event after it counts as censored at it.
``prediction_horizon`` (MS6): the time predicted risks are scored and calibrated at; it changes
no row.

SetForms-Input.title: SetForms
SetForms-Input.description:
The form question's one-tap answer (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a form for
each listed column, the exposure's and its continuous confounders', each checked and completed
as its own ``set_exposure_form`` would be.

SetForms-Output.title: SetForms
SetForms-Output.description:
The form question's one-tap answer (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a form for
each listed column, the exposure's and its continuous confounders', each checked and completed
as its own ``set_exposure_form`` would be.

SetMeasurementError-Input.title: SetMeasurementError
SetMeasurementError-Input.description:
Whether the intakes the recalls measure are corrected for day-to-day error, by regression
calibration declared as a secondary analysis (MS5; audit IN-22, Freedman et al. 2011).
``adjustment`` is filled by the server from the state, never by the client.

SetMeasurementError-Output.title: SetMeasurementError
SetMeasurementError-Output.description:
Whether the intakes the recalls measure are corrected for day-to-day error, by regression
calibration declared as a secondary analysis (MS5; audit IN-22, Freedman et al. 2011).
``adjustment`` is filled by the server from the state, never by the client.

SetMissing-Input.title: SetMissing
SetMissing-Input.description:
How missing predictor values are handled.

``drop_columns`` leave the predictors first (a mostly blank column that means "not asked"),
and the strategy applies to the predictors that remain; the cohort and the design read both.

SetMissing-Output.title: SetMissing
SetMissing-Output.description:
How missing predictor values are handled.

``drop_columns`` leave the predictors first (a mostly blank column that means "not asked"),
and the strategy applies to the predictors that remain; the cohort and the design read both.

SetModification-Input.title: SetModification
SetModification-Input.description:
Declare (or, with ``withdraw``, take back) an effect modifier or a second exposure. A
withdrawal after the estimates were seen (``post_hoc``, set by the server from the plan lock)
leaves the modifier unestimated but counted in the family of tests.

SetModification-Output.title: SetModification
SetModification-Output.description:
Declare (or, with ``withdraw``, take back) an effect modifier or a second exposure. A
withdrawal after the estimates were seen (``post_hoc``, set by the server from the plan lock)
leaves the modifier unestimated but counted in the family of tests.

SetMultiplicity-Input.title: SetMultiplicity
SetMultiplicity-Input.description:
How an exposure family's tests are adjusted (``turbotab.core.methods.omics``):
Benjamini–Hochberg q-values (implied when unanswered), unadjusted with the number of tests
stated (a few prespecified hypotheses), or none; the last two beyond a few tests only with the
recorded attestation (``acknowledged``).

SetMultiplicity-Output.title: SetMultiplicity
SetMultiplicity-Output.description:
How an exposure family's tests are adjusted (``turbotab.core.methods.omics``):
Benjamini–Hochberg q-values (implied when unanswered), unadjusted with the number of tests
stated (a few prespecified hypotheses), or none; the last two beyond a few tests only with the
recorded attestation (``acknowledged``).

SetOrientation.title: SetOrientation
SetOrientation.description: Which way round an assay table is; feature-major is transposed before any diagnosis.

SetOutcomeOrder.title: SetOutcomeOrder
SetOutcomeOrder.description:
The order of an ordinal outcome's levels, lowest first. Stands only while ``column`` is the
target. Numbers are ordered by value without it; text levels need it (asked, never inferred).

SetOutcomeScale.title: SetOutcomeScale
SetOutcomeScale.description:
The scale the outcome ``column`` is analyzed on. "log" makes ``ln_<column>`` the outcome
(the target slot), so every stage, score and sentence reads the column it names; "original"
keeps ``column``, its estimand a difference in means.

SetOutcomeUnit.title: SetOutcomeUnit
SetOutcomeUnit.description:
The outcome's unit, as the user reads it from the source's data dictionary. Stands only
while ``column`` is the target. A unit the name does not spell out is never guessed into a
sentence (audit IN-05; CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §A1.1: "TurboTab will not guess").

SetRoles-Input.title: SetRoles
SetRoles-Input.description:
The confirmed reading of every column except the outcome.

``unconfirmed`` is the server's, never the client's (BLUEPRINT §14 rule 2): the proposals below
high confidence this answer records exactly as proposed, read from the roles the server showed.
A bulk confirm records them, and no number-changing default reads them until each has its own
``confirm_role``.

SetRoles-Output.title: SetRoles
SetRoles-Output.description:
The confirmed reading of every column except the outcome.

``unconfirmed`` is the server's, never the client's (BLUEPRINT §14 rule 2): the proposals below
high confidence this answer records exactly as proposed, read from the roles the server showed.
A bulk confirm records them, and no number-changing default reads them until each has its own
``confirm_role``.

SetScales-Input.title: SetScales
SetScales-Input.description:
The multi-item scales scored as predictors (MS8): each one's items become one score in the
models. An empty list is the answer "no scale is scored".

SetScales-Output.title: SetScales
SetScales-Output.description:
The multi-item scales scored as predictors (MS8): each one's items become one score in the
models. An empty list is the answer "no scale is scored".

SetSensitivity-Input.title: SetSensitivity
SetSensitivity-Input.description:
Analyses beside the primary, each on the rows its own exclusion rules keep (audit ME-16).

Banna et al. 2017: "analyses in the total sample without exclusion of participants should
also be conducted and reported". An empty list is the answer "no sensitivity analysis".

SetSensitivity-Output.title: SetSensitivity
SetSensitivity-Output.description:
Analyses beside the primary, each on the rows its own exclusion rules keep (audit ME-16).

Banna et al. 2017: "analyses in the total sample without exclusion of participants should
also be conducted and reported". An empty list is the answer "no sensitivity analysis".

SetSubstitution-Input.title: SetSubstitution
SetSubstitution-Input.description: The substitution to draw; ``n_boot > 0`` adds a band from that many bootstrap refits.

SetSubstitution-Output.title: SetSubstitution
SetSubstitution-Output.description: The substitution to draw; ``n_boot > 0`` adds a band from that many bootstrap refits.

SetSurvey-Input.title: SetSurvey
SetSurvey-Input.description: Whose estimate it is under a survey design (``SurveySpec``).

SetSurvey-Output.title: SetSurvey
SetSurvey-Output.description: Whose estimate it is under a survey design (``SurveySpec``).

SetTask.title: SetTask
SetTask.description:
An override of task detection, for the outcome column it names.

It stands only while ``column`` is the target (see :func:`fold`).

SetUnit.title: SetUnit
SetUnit.description: When a unit repeats: is one row of the analysis a unit (combined) or a record?

SetUsualIntake-Input.title: SetUsualIntake
SetUsualIntake-Input.description:
One dietary component's usual-intake distribution by the NCI method, or ``model="none"``
(turbotab/core/usual_intake.py). ``nutrient`` names it: a long table's column, or the label of
a wide table's ``days``.

SetUsualIntake-Output.title: SetUsualIntake
SetUsualIntake-Output.description:
One dietary component's usual-intake distribution by the NCI method, or ``model="none"``
(turbotab/core/usual_intake.py). ``nutrient`` names it: a long table's column, or the label of
a wide table's ``days``.

Source.title: Source
Source.description:
A source a declaration cites: a key into ``models.sources.SOURCES`` (MODEL_FAMILY_CONTRACT
§7's verified list, until SIZING X4's citation registry), and where in it.

SurveySpec.title: SurveySpec
SurveySpec.description:
The survey answer: the surveyed population (design-based, ``weight`` and the design named),
or these participants (unweighted, recorded as such; ``turbotab/core/methods/survey.py``).

Sweep.title: Sweep
Sweep.description: The stage's one Confirm sweep: how many defaults it holds, and whether each is answered.

TableFocusView.title: TableFocusView
TableFocusView.description: The working table narrowed to the columns this choice touches (≤ 12 shown, ≤ 8 rows).

Waiting.title: Waiting
Waiting.description: A question a line waits for: its key, its stage and how the app names it.

Where.title: Where
Where.description: Where an item is answered: a record sentence, an analysis paragraph, or a bundle file.

AdjustmentCard.description: WP17 (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 3): the disjunctive cause criterion, asked per covariate.
AdjustmentCard.title: AdjustmentCard

AdjustmentGroup.description: Covariates the pack guesses alike, confirmed with one tap (``decision``); or the unguessed.
AdjustmentGroup.title: AdjustmentGroup

AdjustmentTerm.description:
A coefficient that is not an effect estimate (ESTIMAND; Westreich & Greenland 2013): an
adjustment term, the intercept or a modifier's main effect, with why. Served apart from the
exposure's rows, under the title ``models/effects.py`` gives the appendix.
AdjustmentTerm.title: AdjustmentTerm

AggregationMenu.description: The domain-shaped menu: repeats → mean recommended with its reason; time points → none.
AggregationMenu.title: AggregationMenu

AggregationReceipt.description: What combining did: rows → units, how the outcome was kept, what lost information.
AggregationReceipt.title: AggregationReceipt

ApplyRepair.description:
Apply one of a finding's repair options. Row-local repairs rewrite the working table now;
statistical ones are recorded and executed in-fold (lockbox constitution §06).
ApplyRepair.title: ApplyRepair

AtOpening.description:
The held-out scores recorded when the current outcome's seal was first opened: the reported
result, whatever is drawn, fitted or opened later (audit WP16, RO-05). Set by the server.
AtOpening.title: AtOpening

BandEstimate.description: A measured estimate of what adding a band would cost: one refit per family, timed.
BandEstimate.title: BandEstimate

Baseline.description:
What predicting without the predictors scores on the same folds (M1_CONTRACT §12.6).

The outcome's training-fold mean for regression; the training-fold class prior for
classification. ``value`` is its cross-validated ``metric`` (the primary metric), estimated
as the models' is: a pooled R² of the training-fold mean is 0 by construction.
Baseline.title: Baseline

BatchFigure.description:
The figure ComBat with the outcome protected serves under inference, never a test (the batch
answer's ``figures``; ``methods/batch.py``): principal components before and after it.
BatchFigure.title: BatchFigure

BatchFigurePoint.description:
One row of the batch figure: its batch, its outcome, and its first two principal-component
scores before and after ComBat with the outcome protected.
BatchFigurePoint.title: BatchFigurePoint

BeeswarmInput.description:
One input's points: its SHAP value, its value (None for a category or a blank), and its
value's percentile among the explained rows for the color (a category: its level's place).
BeeswarmInput.title: BeeswarmInput

BrantCheck.description: Brant's (1990) Wald test of the proportional-odds assumption: overall, and per column.
BrantCheck.title: BrantCheck

CalibratedContrast.description: The substitution as the difference of calibrated coefficients (all-components).
CalibratedContrast.title: CalibratedContrast

CalibratedExposure.description: One error-prone column: its uncorrected and its calibrated coefficient.
CalibratedExposure.title: CalibratedExposure

Calibration.description: Calibration of one set of predictions: in the large, its slope, and its smoothed curve.

smoother.default: lowess, span 2/3, no robustness iterations (as rms val.prob)
smoother.title: Smoother

Calibration.title: Calibration

label.default: corrects only within-person random error, assuming recalls are unbiased for usual intake (customary; sound under that assumption)
label.title: Label

test.default: The test of no association is the uncorrected model's: “the usual statistical test of the null hypothesis (no exposure effect) remains theoretically valid” (Freedman et al. 2011, J Natl Cancer Inst 103:1086); the calibrated estimate gives the size, with its own interval.
test.title: Test

CategoricalProposal.description: A predictor whose numbers may be codes for groups (``set_categorical`` declares it).
CategoricalProposal.title: CategoricalProposal

CausalSelection.description: What the post-double-selection lassos chose, by raw column, and the model terms kept.
CausalSelection.title: CausalSelection

ChainLink.description: A relation that fired on this fit: because ``because``, ``then`` (BLUEPRINT §13).
ChainLink.title: ChainLink

Chronology.description:
The chronological draw the temporal answer asked for, and whether it was drawn.

Whole units are held out by their last observation, so with repeated rows a held-out unit's
earlier rows can predate training rows (audit IN-24: 56–71% of held-out rows on visit data).
``n_held_rows``/``n_held_earlier`` count that for this draw; ``earlier`` for each share the
split question offers, at this draw's seed, so the split's sentence can state it.
Chronology.title: Chronology

ClusterScore.description: One held-out cluster: its rows, its scores, and the primary metric's interval.
ClusterScore.title: ClusterScore

CodebookConflict.description:
A codebook field the values contradict, or one whose check cannot run here (``checked``
False: a check that cannot run confirms nothing): asked, never applied (BLUEPRINT
§14.2–§14.3).
CodebookConflict.title: CodebookConflict

CohortArtifact.description: The ``cohort`` artifact (a Bundle's ``data``): the participant flow.
CohortArtifact.title: CohortArtifact

CombinedColumn.description: One column that varied within a unit (or was given its own rule), and how it was combined.
CombinedColumn.title: CombinedColumn

Comparison.description: MS6: the repeated k-fold the families and the baseline are compared on (models/folds.py).
Comparison.title: Comparison

CompleteCaseLoss.description: What complete cases cost: the rows dropped beside the rows kept (audit WP7, E14).
CompleteCaseLoss.title: CompleteCaseLoss

CovariateAnswers.description:
The modified disjunctive cause criterion, asked as questions (VanderWeele 2019; MODELING_
SEQUENCE §1 step 3). The covariate's role is derived from these, never chosen directly.
CovariateAnswers.title: CovariateAnswers

Customary.description:
Where the field uses the option: ``text`` says how, ``field`` in which field, ``source``
where that is documented.
Customary.title: Customary

DeclaredResult.description: What the fit reports as the result, and on what basis (module docstring).
DeclaredResult.title: DeclaredResult

DerivedColumn.description: A column the working table derives row by row (the log-scale outcome; audit RO-10).
DerivedColumn.title: DerivedColumn

DesignArtifact.description: The ``design`` artifact: each model's pipeline and the columns it will see.
DesignArtifact.title: DesignArtifact

Diagnosed.description:
What the diagnostics were computed for: the lane's parts and the key of those parts and the
rows (:func:`diagnostics_key`). A declaration made after them carries the key.
Diagnosed.title: Diagnosed

EarlierRows.description:
For one held-out share drawn by time: how many held-out rows there are, and how many were
observed before the latest training row (audit IN-24).
EarlierRows.title: EarlierRows

EnergyRanking.description:
The energy methods in order of soundness for the declared purpose, applicable ones first
(audit WP6; BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 2): the all-components model first under inference, the
energy-keeping models first under prediction. ``line`` names the tension with custom.
EnergyRanking.title: EnergyRanking

EnergyReading.description: What the energy-adjustment question can offer on this table (NUTRITION_PACK §04).
EnergyReading.title: EnergyReading

EnergyUnitReading.description: The energy column's unit and how it was read (audit IN-07).
EnergyUnitReading.title: EnergyUnitReading

EstimandAnnotation.description:
WP17: the served fit under a declared estimand (``turbotab/core/estimand.py``): the caption
worded from it, and which table rows are the exposure's effect; the rest are adjustment terms.
EstimandAnnotation.title: EstimandAnnotation

EstimandCard.description: WP17 (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 step 2): what the exposure and effect question offers.
EstimandCard.title: EstimandCard

EstimandFamily.description: Every exposure reported in turn (the feature-wise family), with its multiplicity method.
EstimandFamily.title: EstimandFamily

ExclusionProposal.description: One of the pack's exclusion rules, with the rows it would remove. Never pre-selected.
ExclusionProposal.title: ExclusionProposal

ExposureFormOption.description:
One form an exposure can enter the model in (WP12a; ``turbotab/core/methods/exposure_form.py``
``options``), with north star 5's two labels, in the order of soundness for the purpose.
ExposureFormOption.title: ExposureFormOption

ExposureFormSpec.description:
How one numeric predictor enters the models: a straight line, a restricted cubic spline
(``knots`` 3–5, at Harrell's percentiles; ``knots_rule`` "harrell" when k was set by the
declared rule on ``n_effective``), quintile indicators with a trend test, indicators at declared
cut points (``cuts``), one data-derived cut point, or, for an exposure with a mass at zero,
non-consumers as their own category beside a spline among consumers. ``domain`` "consumers"
restricts the analysis to consumers (an estimand change, STROBE-nut nut-14). ``acknowledged``
keeps a blocked-and-recorded form as a recorded limitation. ``scale`` is the exposure's
transform as it stood when the form was declared (``methods.exposure_form.transform_signature``):
a later transform makes the form stale, re-asked and never kept. ``unit`` is the unit the
estimate is per, on that scale (the estimand's unit).
ExposureFormSpec.title: ExposureFormSpec

ExposureTest.description:
A test an exposure's form carries under inference (``methods/exposure_form.py``): a
spline's overall and nonlinear Wald tests, or quintiles' trend across their medians.
ExposureTest.title: ExposureTest

FamilyDifference.description:
Two families' primary metric, paired over the same folds of the comparison substrate, with
the corrected repeated k-fold t (module docstring).
FamilyDifference.title: FamilyDifference

FitArtifact.description: The ``fit`` artifact: cross-validated and held-out performance per model.
FitArtifact.title: FitArtifact

Floor.description:
The held-out performance floor: the family's cross-validated score against the
no-predictor baseline's on the same folds (``models/baseline.py``).
Floor.title: Floor

FollowUpCandidate.description: A column that reads as how long each row was followed (``turbotab/core/estimand.py``).
FollowUpCandidate.title: FollowUpCandidate

FormNeed.description: One column the form question asks about.
FormNeed.title: FormNeed

FormWaiting.description:
A column the question would ask about if it holds amounts, while its code-or-amount reading
is unsettled: the reading is asked first (the question's ask card), and no form is proposed.
FormWaiting.title: FormWaiting

FormsArtifact.description: The ``forms`` stage: the functional-form question's card (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5).
FormsArtifact.title: FormsArtifact

GoldbergRule.description:
Keep rows whose reported energy intake over estimated BMR lies within the Goldberg cut-offs
(Goldberg et al. 1991, revised by Black 2000): ``PAL × exp(±2 S / 100)`` at n = 1, with
``S = √(CV²_wEI / d + CV²_wB + CV²_tP)``. Every input is stated: the BMR equation, the PAL (one
value, or one per level of an activity column), and the days of intake the energy averages.
GoldbergRule.title: GoldbergRule

HoldoutDetail.description: What the held-out rows say beyond their scores: an interval on each, and calibration.
HoldoutDetail.title: HoldoutDetail

HorizonCalibration.description: Calibration of a time-to-event model's risks by a horizon (module docstring).
HorizonCalibration.title: HorizonCalibration

ImportCodebook.description:
Import the researcher's own data dictionary (Nolan, 2026-10-03; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a
variable/label/unit/codes table, an NHANES codebook page, or the labels an XPT file carries.
Its structured fields (units, value-code tables, the variable type) settle readings as the
user's own documentation, through the confirmation path ``confirm_readings`` writes; its
free-text labels only strengthen the guesses the ask leads with; a field the values contradict
is asked, never applied. The client names the staged codebook; everything else is the
server's, read from the codebook and the values.
ImportCodebook.title: ImportCodebook

Inference.description:
How the coefficient table's intervals were made (AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP2;
``turbotab/core/models/inference.py``): the estimator, the covariance, and the clusters.
Inference.title: Inference

InferenceExit.description: A way forward when no interval can be reported, as a refusal's exits are shaped.
InferenceExit.title: InferenceExit

InputCurves.description: One input's curve for every family, on one grid (shared axes).
InputCurves.title: InputCurves

InputImportance.description: One input's mean |SHAP|, its rank, and its rank in each reseeded refit.
InputImportance.title: InputImportance

Interval.description: A score with its standard error and its 95% interval.
Interval.title: Interval

JoinCounts.description:
What the join's preview counted, recorded with the answer (the server's): the rows on each
side, the identifier values they share, the rows with no partner on each side, and the rows
the joined table holds.
JoinCounts.title: JoinCounts

JoinFiles.description:
Join a file added to the project to the table on a shared identifier (NHANES ships each
component as its own file, joined on ``SEQN``). ``how``: ``left`` keeps every row of the
table (a row with no partner holds blanks in the file's columns), ``inner`` only the rows with
one. One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-one are joined; many-to-many is refused with its
reason. ``name`` and ``counts`` are the server's, never the client's: the preview's counts,
recorded with the answer.
JoinFiles.title: JoinFiles

LabeledChoice.description: An option with north star 5's two labels (as ``custom_sound`` shapes them).
LabeledChoice.title: LabeledChoice

LabeledQuestion.description:
A question's options, soundest first for the purpose, each with its two labels, and the one
line naming the tension when the field's customary first choice is not the soundest.
LabeledQuestion.title: LabeledQuestion

LeaveOut.description: The offer: leave the likely-not-asked columns out, then handle the rest.
LeaveOut.title: LeaveOut

LevelCalibration.description: One level's calibration: an ordinal cut-point ("at or above") or a multiclass class.
LevelCalibration.title: LevelCalibration

LockPlan.description:
The inference analysis-plan lock (audit WP16, RO-12; MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 12).

Recorded by the server when Fit is pressed (SIZING P0.8; before P0.8, when inference
estimates were first displayed), never posted by a client: the plan in force then is what was
declared in the software before any estimate was displayed, and every later decision is marked
as made after the estimates were seen. ``plan``
(every slot the estimates read, as it stood) and ``digest`` (its SHA-256) are filled by the
server. A client never undoes it; the server withdraws it (a revert it records itself) only
while no estimate has been served under it, on Cancel or a change to the plan
(calm/FOUNDATION §7), and the next press of Fit records a new one.
LockPlan.title: LockPlan

MetricSummary.description:
One metric's cross-validated score (``turbotab/core/models/metrics.py``).

``estimate`` is the score the app reports: pooled over every out-of-fold prediction for R²,
RMSE and MAE (``estimator: "pooled"``), the mean over folds otherwise (``"fold_mean"``).
``mean`` and ``sd`` describe the per-fold values, which show the spread.
MetricSummary.title: MetricSummary

MissingColumn.description: A predictor with blanks, counted among rows with the outcome measured.
MissingColumn.title: MissingColumn

MissingData.description:
How the inference table handled missing predictor values (AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP7, ME-01;
``turbotab/core/methods/missing.py``): multiple imputation with the outcome (m imputations by
chained equations, pooled by Rubin's rules), complete cases with their assumption, or a single
fill kept with its recorded attestation.
MissingData.title: MissingData

MissingMethodOption.description:
A way to handle missing values (or values below detection), with its two labels (north star
5) and its rung for the declared purpose (audit WP7; ``turbotab/core/methods/missing.py``).
MissingMethodOption.title: MissingMethodOption

MissingReading.description: What the missing-values question can offer on this table (M1_CONTRACT §12.4).
MissingReading.title: MissingReading

ModelSequenceCard.description: ESTIMAND (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 11): Model 1's declaration, the pack's guess leading.
ModelSequenceCard.title: ModelSequenceCard

MultiplicityQuestion.description: ESTIMAND (MODELING_SEQUENCE §2): an exposure family's multiplicity method.
MultiplicityQuestion.title: MultiplicityQuestion

NestedCV.description: Bates, Hastie & Tibshirani's nested cross-validation interval for one family's primary.
NestedCV.title: NestedCV

NestedColumn.description: A predictor that is part of another (``fat_sat`` of ``fat_total``), confirmed on training rows.
NestedColumn.title: NestedColumn

NestedOffer.description: MS6: the nested cross-validation interval, offered where predictors outnumber rows.
NestedOffer.title: NestedOffer

NotAdjusted.description: An exposure energy adjustment leaves as it is, and why (it carries no energy, it is a share).
NotAdjusted.title: NotAdjusted

Observations.description: Per-row attributions: ``base + Σ phi + rest == prediction`` on the model's scale.
Observations.title: Observations

OmittedEnergy.description: How much of total energy a model's energy-bearing columns leave out (audit ME-05).
OmittedEnergy.title: OmittedEnergy

OpenSeal.description:
Open the held-out rows: once, at the end. Held-out scores are withheld until then.

``family`` is the final model, declared on cross-validation before any held-out score is seen
(AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP8, ME-13; ``turbotab/core/models/selection.py``): its held-out score is the
reported result. Required when several families are fitted; with one, the opening declares it.
Null only in records from before the rule.
OpenSeal.title: OpenSeal

Optimism.description: Harrell's bootstrap optimism correction of one family (module docstring).
Optimism.title: Optimism

OrientationReading.description: Question 1.5's shape reading: row-mean spread over column-mean spread, on a log scale.
OrientationReading.title: OrientationReading

OrientedArtifact.description: The ``oriented`` artifact: the raw table or its transpose (DatasetInfo of the result).
OrientedArtifact.title: OrientedArtifact

OutcomeDispute.description:
An energy-related outcome's DISPUTED note for the energy card (audit IN-20; NUTRITION_PACK
§04: "escalate the mediation/collider warning"): what the outcome's name reads as, the card
line (also in ``notes``) and its badge.
OutcomeDispute.title: OutcomeDispute

Pooled.description: A DerSimonian–Laird random-effects summary of one score across clusters.
Pooled.title: Pooled

ProposalsArtifact.description: The ``proposals`` artifact: offered for the exclusions, missing-values and energy questions.
ProposalsArtifact.title: ProposalsArtifact

Quantity.description:
One reported quantity: on a ratio scale ``estimate`` is the ratio (the RERI its own value);
on a difference scale the difference.
Quantity.title: Quantity

QuestionLabels.description:
WP17 (north star 5): each question's options with "customary in <field>" and "sound for
<purpose>", soundest first (``turbotab/core/custom_sound.py``).
QuestionLabels.title: QuestionLabels

ReferenceRowsLeft.description: Rows a recorded repair excluded as reference rows (pooled QC injections; audit RO-13).
ReferenceRowsLeft.title: ReferenceRowsLeft

RepairOption.description: One way to act on a finding, and the ``apply_repair`` it records.
RepairOption.title: RepairOption

RepeatsReading.description: Repeats or time points, read from date spacing or a record index (turbotab/repeats.py).
RepeatsReading.title: RepeatsReading

Reseal.description:
Draw the held-out rows again after they were opened (audit WP16, RO-05).

Once opened, the held-out rows hold still: a new seed or holdout, or anything else that would
draw them again, waits for this recorded re-seal. It withdraws the opening of the current
outcome's seal, so the rows drawn next are withheld until they are opened in turn; the scores
at the first opening stay the reported result, and later held-out scores are not an
independent test. ``target`` is filled by the server. It stands while its outcome is the
target, as the opening does.
Reseal.title: Reseal

RolesArtifact.description: The ``roles`` artifact: a proposed role for every column but the outcome.
RolesArtifact.title: RolesArtifact

RowComparison.description: One column on the rows complete cases kept and on those they dropped (audit E14).
RowComparison.title: RowComparison

SampleSize.description: Riley et al.'s minimum sample size, computed before the shelf is ranked (TRIPOD+AI 10).
SampleSize.title: SampleSize

ScaleQuestion.description:
The scale a positive, markedly skewed outcome is analyzed on
(``turbotab.core.structural.scale_question``).
ScaleQuestion.title: ScaleQuestion

ScaleSpec.description:
One scale: its items, the instrument's key (the reverse-coded items and the response scale
``low``–``high`` they are turned over on), how the score is formed, what kind of construct it
measures (``reflective``: the items are caused by it; ``formative``: an index defined by its
components, such as a diet-quality score), its structure, the role the score takes in the
models, and whether its coefficient is corrected for measurement error, from which reliability.
ScaleSpec.title: ScaleSpec

SealBasis.description: How the held-out rows were drawn: one of four states, never inferred silently.
SealBasis.title: SealBasis

SealFloor.description: Below this many held-out rows (or events), cross-validation alone is offered first.
SealFloor.title: SealFloor

SealPlan.description: The ``seal_plan`` artifact: what the split question can offer on this table.
SealPlan.title: SealPlan

Selection.description:
What choosing among families on cross-validation costs (``models/selection.py``): the best
family's CV score flatters it, by about ``optimism``, estimated by bootstrap bias-corrected
cross-validation over the families' out-of-fold predictions (Tsamardinos et al. 2018).
Selection.title: Selection

SensitivityAnalysis.description: One analysis beside the primary: the same model on the rows these rules keep instead.
SensitivityAnalysis.title: SensitivityAnalysis

enum: eligible rows outside the held-out set
rows.title: Rows

SensitivityChange.description: How an exposure's estimate moves across the analyses, against the primary's.
SensitivityChange.title: SensitivityChange

SensitivityRow.description: One analysis: its rules (as the participant flow labels them) and the rows they keep.
SensitivityRow.title: SensitivityRow

SetAdjustment.description:
Answers for some covariates, against one exposure: one tap per group of covariates that
share their answers (BLUEPRINT §14.2). Each covariate's answer is kept under its column, so a
later group's answers never undo an earlier group's.
SetAdjustment.title: SetAdjustment

SetBatch.description:
How a batch column is handled, by purpose (``turbotab.core.methods.batch``). ``figures``
adds ComBat with the outcome protected for figures only: never the matrix the tests read.
SetBatch.title: SetBatch

SetCensoring.description:
The follow-up question's "no" (audit RO-03): nobody's follow-up ended before the event could
be seen, so the yes/no outcome counts events over one period for everyone. Stands only while
``column`` is the target. Follow-up that varies is a time to event instead (``set_task``, then
``set_follow_up``). ``acknowledged``: kept although a column reads as a follow-up time that
varies (block and record).
SetCensoring.title: SetCensoring

SetClusters.description:
The grouping above the person (audit RO-08). The answer is also each named column's
``cluster`` reading (BLUEPRINT §14.3): a grouping confirms it, "nothing groups them" denies
each column that read as one (``none_of``, filled by the server), and a later confirmation of
that reading stands over it, as the answer stands over an earlier one.
SetClusters.title: SetClusters

SetColumnUnit.description:
A column's unit, as the user reads it from the source's data dictionary, where TurboTab
could only propose one: total energy in kcal or kJ (a day's, or a total over ``days`` days),
or an age in years, months, weeks or days. Leash (BLUEPRINT §11.3): a unit not read from a
stated suffix, a codebook or the values' own agreement is a proposal, and no screen, band or
count is applied in it until it is recorded here.
SetColumnUnit.title: SetColumnUnit

SetExclusions.description: Row exclusions; an empty list is the answer "keep every row".
SetExclusions.title: SetExclusions

SetExposureForm.description:
The form of one predictor (``turbotab.core.methods.exposure_form``); one entry per column.
Left without ``knots``, a spline takes k by the declared rule on the analyzed rows (the
completion records it); ``scale`` and ``unit`` are the server's.
SetExposureForm.title: SetExposureForm

SetFeatureTable.description:
How a features-in-rows table reads: the column naming the features, and the columns that
describe them (m/z, retention time, IDs). Turning it makes every other column a sample.
SetFeatureTable.title: SetFeatureTable

SetFollowUp.description:
The follow-up of a time-to-event outcome. Stands only while ``column`` is the target.

``landmark``: follow-up counted from this time on (a landmark, or the customary "the first
years of follow-up excluded" for reverse causation): a row whose follow-up ended at or before
it, by an event or not, was not at risk then and leaves, and every other row is at risk from
it (left truncation; the estimate is among those event-free and followed at the landmark).
``horizon``: follow-up ends at this time: an event after it counts as censored at it.
``prediction_horizon`` (MS6): the time predicted risks are scored and calibrated at; it changes
no row.
SetFollowUp.title: SetFollowUp

SetForms.description:
The form question's one-tap answer (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 5; BLUEPRINT §14.2): a form for
each listed column, the exposure's and its continuous confounders', each checked and completed
as its own ``set_exposure_form`` would be.
SetForms.title: SetForms

SetMeasurementError.description:
Whether the intakes the recalls measure are corrected for day-to-day error, by regression
calibration declared as a secondary analysis (MS5; audit IN-22, Freedman et al. 2011).
``adjustment`` is filled by the server from the state, never by the client.
SetMeasurementError.title: SetMeasurementError

SetMissing.description:
How missing predictor values are handled.

``drop_columns`` leave the predictors first (a mostly blank column that means "not asked"),
and the strategy applies to the predictors that remain; the cohort and the design read both.
SetMissing.title: SetMissing

SetModification.description:
Declare (or, with ``withdraw``, take back) an effect modifier or a second exposure. A
withdrawal after the estimates were seen (``post_hoc``, set by the server from the plan lock)
leaves the modifier unestimated but counted in the family of tests.
SetModification.title: SetModification

SetMultiplicity.description:
How an exposure family's tests are adjusted (``turbotab.core.methods.omics``):
Benjamini–Hochberg q-values (implied when unanswered), unadjusted with the number of tests
stated (a few prespecified hypotheses), or none; the last two beyond a few tests only with the
recorded attestation (``acknowledged``).
SetMultiplicity.title: SetMultiplicity

SetRoles.description:
The confirmed reading of every column except the outcome.

``unconfirmed`` is the server's, never the client's (BLUEPRINT §14 rule 2): the proposals below
high confidence this answer records exactly as proposed, read from the roles the server showed.
A bulk confirm records them, and no number-changing default reads them until each has its own
``confirm_role``.
SetRoles.title: SetRoles

SetScales.description:
The multi-item scales scored as predictors (MS8): each one's items become one score in the
models. An empty list is the answer "no scale is scored".
SetScales.title: SetScales

SetSensitivity.description:
Analyses beside the primary, each on the rows its own exclusion rules keep (audit ME-16).

Banna et al. 2017: "analyses in the total sample without exclusion of participants should
also be conducted and reported". An empty list is the answer "no sensitivity analysis".
SetSensitivity.title: SetSensitivity

SetSubstitution.description: The substitution to draw; ``n_boot > 0`` adds a band from that many bootstrap refits.
SetSubstitution.title: SetSubstitution

SetSurvey.description: Whose estimate it is under a survey design (``SurveySpec``).
SetSurvey.title: SetSurvey

SetUsualIntake.description:
One dietary component's usual-intake distribution by the NCI method, or ``model="none"``
(turbotab/core/usual_intake.py). ``nutrient`` names it: a long table's column, or the label of
a wide table's ``days``.
SetUsualIntake.title: SetUsualIntake

ShelfArtifact.description: The ``shelf`` artifact: every family that can model the task, best first.
ShelfArtifact.title: ShelfArtifact

SimulationCost.description:
What the g-formula will take at the default size, measured on these rows, and the parts
that scale with each count (``models.time_varying.gformula_cost``).
SimulationCost.title: SimulationCost

Sound.description: Whether the option is sound for ``purpose``, and why.
Sound.title: Sound

SplitArtifact.description: The ``split`` artifact (a Bundle's ``data``): held-out rows and folds.
SplitArtifact.title: SplitArtifact

Stability.description: Mean |SHAP| over the same rows, refit on bootstrap resamples each with its own seed.
Stability.title: Stability

StatedGrain.description:
The grain stated rather than asked (M2_CONTRACT §10): a recognized person identifier that is
unique on every row, with nothing else repeating like a roster. "Ask me anyway" reopens it.
StatedGrain.title: StatedGrain

StructureArtifact.description: The ``structure`` artifact: what the grain, repeats, unit and aggregation questions offer.
StructureArtifact.title: StructureArtifact

SubstitutionArtifact.description: The ``substitution`` artifact: one curve per fitted model.
SubstitutionArtifact.title: SubstitutionArtifact

SubstitutionBand.description: How the band was made: refits of every family on bootstrap resamples of training rows.
SubstitutionBand.title: SubstitutionBand

SubstitutionSupport.description: Which rows each k averages over, and how many each support check left out (per k).
SubstitutionSupport.title: SubstitutionSupport

SurveyInference.description:
The survey design a design-based table rests on (AUDIT_REPORT §5 WP10;
``turbotab/core/models/survey.py``): what weighted it, its PSUs and strata, the domain.
SurveyInference.title: SurveyInference

SurveyOption.description: One answer the survey question offers, and the ``set_survey`` it records (audit §5 WP10).
SurveyOption.title: SurveyOption

SurveyProposal.description:
What the survey question offers on this table: the design the column names read as, the
cycles a cycle column pools, and one option per recognized weight plus "these participants".
SurveyProposal.title: SurveyProposal

TimeOrder.description: Whether the time column can put a unit's records in order (stages.working.time_order).
TimeOrder.title: TimeOrder

TurnCheck.description:
Whether the table can be turned around: the feature-name column, the columns that describe
the features (kept beside them, never turned into samples), and why not.
TurnCheck.title: TurnCheck

ValidationOption.description: One way the training rows can validate the models, as the split question offers it.
ValidationOption.title: ValidationOption

ValidationPlan.description: The validation options in the order to offer them, and why (module docstring).

source.default: Harrell 2017, Split-sample model validation: data splitting is unstable below about 20,000 subjects
source.title: Source

ValidationPlan.title: ValidationPlan

VersusBaseline.description: A family's primary metric against its baseline's, paired over the same folds.
VersusBaseline.title: VersusBaseline

WorkingArtifact.description: The ``working`` artifact: DatasetInfo of the table every later stage reads.
WorkingArtifact.title: WorkingArtifact
